source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables; Instructions PDF p13 Line 6, $5,660 subtraction for taxpayers 65 and older; Form 2 PDF p1 line 6; record base.deductions age_65_subtraction

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 24,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 40,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 15,750.00; line 3 24,250.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 0 x 5,660.00 = 0.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 24,250.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 24,250.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 24,250.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 5.9% x 24,250.00 = 1,430.75, less 253 = 1,177.75; line 13 = 1,177.75, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 21,100.00 = 991.70; 5.9% x (24,250.00 - 21,100.00 = 3,150.00) = 185.85; bracket tax 1,177.55. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 1,177.55. The form gives 1,177.75; expected keeps the projection's 1,177.55, a difference of 0.20 from the table's whole-dollar constant (253 against 253.20). Household income about 40,000.00 and a person 62 or older: the refundable Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit (Form 2 line 16) may apply; it is not in the projection and is left out. Born 1961-01-02: 64 for 2025, so line 6 is 0.00 and the federal additional deduction is not taken either.
accepted_approximations: The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit: refundable, up to 1,150, for age 62 or older with household income under 45,000. Property tax relief outside the record.
